minutes.headline: Stormwater Task Force approved prior minutes and heard updates on GPS drainage mapping and a planned high school rain garden.
minutes.summary: The task force approved its February minutes by roll call, heard a member's review of the Central Mass stormwater coalition and Think Blue websites, and got updates on a SharePoint site, the start of drainage asset data collection, street sweeping and catch basin cleaning, and a demonstration rain garden at the high school. It also noted that a member left when he resigned from the select board, so the group will reorganize in June. It adjourned by roll call.

budget_items.topic: Stormwater cost expenditures through end of March
budget_items.what_was_said: A spreadsheet of stormwater expenditures through March was circulated. February was essentially zero and March was low, with April expected to be larger because of sweeping and culvert work.
Spending for the fiscal year so far was stated and expected to climb with three heavy months of road and stormwater maintenance ahead.
A new equipment operator was hired to start Monday, giving full staff so sweeping and catch basin cleaning can happen at the same time.

budget_items.topic: Engineering funding for demonstration BMP / rain garden
budget_items.what_was_said: There is enough funding in the existing budget for the engineering survey work, and the total stormwater budget was mentioned.

Construction was estimated roughly in the low tens of thousands, with design, media, plants and installation as the main costs, and some work possibly done by staff or students. The demonstration BMP was not specifically budgeted, and an earlier quote had been inflated by a formula error.
A spreadsheet tool for building a stormwater utility was shared, and members said it is for later when funding and a possible fee supporting an enterprise account are considered.
The data collection under the asset management grant is expected to run about two months and will let the town meet an MS4 permit requirement in year 10.

decisions.decision: A member will try the SharePoint site for meeting materials with a volunteer who has only a town email account; members without active accounts were told to contact IT.
Bill will bring estimated cost numbers and a concept sketch for the rain garden to the next meeting.
The task force will continue as is through May and reorganize in June after the select board reorganizes; the next meeting is May 18.
Members interested in coalition trainings or materials will tell staff, who will reproduce them or arrange access.

what_happened.line: The task force approved its February minutes by roll call; no other votes were taken.
Staff said GPS data collection under the asset management grant should take about two months and will let the town meet an MS4 permit requirement.
A demonstration rain garden at the high school was discussed; it was not specifically budgeted, and Bill will bring cost estimates and a concept sketch next meeting.
A new equipment operator starts Monday, giving full staff to run street sweeping and catch basin cleaning at the same time.
The task force will continue as is through May and reorganize in June after the select board reorganizes; the next meeting is May 18.

why_it_matters: Stormwater work is paid from the existing budget for now, and a rain garden or a future stormwater utility fee, which would be a new charge on property owners, would come to residents as a funding question later.
